topic: How Heating and Burning Change Material Properties
key_concepts: Heating can change a material's size, shape, and color
Wood burns to black char and then ash as temperature rises
Coal changes color, size, and flame intensity as temperature rises
At high temperatures coal turns into glowing embers
Burning wood or coal produces smoke, flames, light, and heat
Burning cardboard makes it smaller, irregular, black or gray, and ashy
Heating and cooling can cause reversible changes
Some heat changes are irreversible, such as cooking an egg or burning paper
Melting and refreezing ice cream is a reversible change
Heat sources include fire, electrical appliances, and the sun
Cooling can also change material properties, such as shrinking a rubber band
Different materials respond to heat by melting, expanding, deforming, or changing color
